discovery: Optical lattice clocks: invention and realization of optical atomic clocks with 10^-18 level accuracy

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision metrology
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005): neutral atoms trapped in an optical lattice at a 'magic wavelength' that leaves the clock transition unperturbed, combining the low noise of many atoms with the absence of motional shifts. Ye and his team turned this concept, together with femtosecond frequency-comb technology and ultrastable lasers, into clocks with systematic uncertainty and stability at the 10^-18 level and below, now surpassing caesium standards by two orders of magnitude. These clocks resolve gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, test fundamental constants and dark-matter models, enable relativistic geodesy, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. It is a clean breakthrough in measurement technology that lets us see what no one could see before, emerging from curiosity-driven basic research with deep practical consequences, and achieved through outstanding international collaboration.
